data.howToName: How to scale a recipe from 8 servings to 2
notes: Quartering leaves tiny amounts. Measure them in spoons, not cups.
4 eggs become 1 egg. 3 eggs become 3/4 of an egg, beaten and measured.
Use a much smaller pan and check for doneness early.

description: Scale a recipe that serves 8 down to 2 servings. The factor is 0.25, so every amount is quartered, with small amounts turned into spoons you can measure.

examples.result: The scaled stew serves 2: 1 cup beef, 1/2 cup carrots, 1 cup broth, 1/2 teaspoon salt.
steps: Multiply each amount by 0.25: 4 cups beef become 1 cup, 2 cups carrots become 1/2 cup.
Broth: 4 cups × 0.25 = 1 cup. Salt: 2 teaspoons × 0.25 = 1/2 teaspoon.
examples.title: A stew for 8, scaled down to serve 2

examples.result: The scaled muffins use 1/2 cup flour, 1/4 cup sugar, 1 egg, and 1/2 teaspoon baking powder.
steps: Flour: 2 cups × 0.25 = 1/2 cup. Sugar: 1 cup × 0.25 = 1/4 cup.
Eggs: 4 × 0.25 = 1 egg. Baking powder: 2 teaspoons × 0.25 = 1/2 teaspoon.
examples.title: 8 muffins, scaled down to make 2

faqs.answer: Divide the servings you want by the servings the recipe makes: 2 ÷ 8 = 0.25. Multiply every ingredient by 0.25, which is the same as dividing by 4. The scaler above does it one ingredient at a time.
faqs.question: What is the scale factor from 8 servings to 2?

faqs.answer: Beat the eggs and measure by volume or weight. A large egg is about 3 tablespoons beaten and about 50 g out of the shell. 3 eggs quartered is 3/4 of an egg, which is about 2 1/4 tablespoons or about 38 g.
faqs.question: How do I quarter 3 eggs?

faqs.answer: Convert to spoons. A quarter of a cup is 1 tablespoon. A third of a cup quartered is 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon. A teaspoon quartered is a quarter teaspoon. The table above gives the spoon versions of the common amounts.
faqs.question: How do I measure tiny amounts like a quarter of a cup?

faqs.answer: Use a much smaller pan, about a quarter of the area, so the depth stays the same. A quartered cake in the original pan bakes paper thin and dries out. A small loaf pan or a couple of ramekins often work better than a cake pan.
faqs.question: What size pan do I use for a quartered recipe?

faqs.answer: Yes, usually a little faster. A smaller amount of food in a smaller pan cooks quicker. Start checking about 5 minutes before the original time.
faqs.question: Does a quartered recipe cook faster?

faqs.answer: Yes. Scaling down is kinder than scaling up: nothing overflows, nothing over-leavens, and the only real challenge is measuring small amounts accurately. A scale and a set of measuring spoons solve that.
faqs.question: Is scaling down easier than scaling up?

felicityNote: Eight to two is the batch recipe problem. The recipe feeds a crowd, the table is two people, and a quarter of it is exactly right.

parts.meaning: The multiplier for every ingredient. From 8 to 2 servings, the factor is 0.25.
The number of servings you want to make. Here, 2.
The number of servings the recipe makes as written. Here, 8.

formula.text: Scale factor = desired servings ÷ original servings. Scaled amount = original amount × scale factor. From 8 to 2 servings, the factor is 0.25.

howToSteps.name: Find the factor
howToSteps.text: Divide the servings you want by the servings the recipe makes. 2 ÷ 8 = 0.25, which is a quarter.

howToSteps.name: Quarter each amount
howToSteps.text: Work down the ingredient list and multiply each amount by 0.25. Convert small results to spoons, using the table above.

howToSteps.name: Deal with the eggs
howToSteps.text: 4 eggs become 1 egg. An odd count leaves a fraction of an egg: beat the eggs and measure by the tablespoon, about 3 tablespoons per egg.

howToSteps.name: Quarter the leavening too
howToSteps.text: Baking powder and baking soda quarter exactly. Unlike scaling up, there is no adjustment needed when you scale down.

howToSteps.name: Use a much smaller pan
howToSteps.text: Pick a pan about a quarter of the area so the depth stays the same. Check for doneness early, because a small batch cooks faster.

lede: A recipe for 8 cut down to 2 has a scale factor of 0.25. Multiply every ingredient by 0.25 and measure the small results in spoons.

title: Scale a Recipe from 8 Servings to 2
tutorial: Eight to two is the batch recipe problem. The recipe was written for a crowd, or for a week of meal prep, and tonight the table is two people. The factor is 0.25: 2 divided by 8. Every ingredient gets quartered, which is easy maths and fiddly measuring. One cup becomes a quarter cup. A tablespoon becomes three quarters of a teaspoon. The numbers are small, and small numbers need spoons, not cups.

Eggs are the decision point. Four eggs quarter cleanly to 1 egg. Three eggs quarter to three quarters of an egg, which means beating the eggs and measuring. A large egg is about 3 tablespoons beaten and about 50 g out of the shell, so three quarters of an egg is about 2 1/4 tablespoons, or about 38 g on a scale. It feels fussy, but it is the difference between a bake that sets and one that does not.

The pan matters more at this scale than at any other. A quartered recipe in the original pan spreads thin and dries out, or overcooks before you notice. Use a pan about a quarter of the area: a small loaf pan, a couple of ramekins, or an 8 inch square pan instead of a 9 by 13. And check for doneness early, because a small batch cooks faster than the recipe says.

Scaling down is kinder than scaling up in every other way. Leavening quarters exactly, with no adjustment. Salt and spices quarter exactly. Nothing overflows and nothing over-leavens. The only real challenge is measuring small amounts accurately, and a kitchen scale plus a set of measuring spoons solves that. A quarter teaspoon measure and an eighth teaspoon measure earn their drawer space here.

There is one more option worth considering: cook the full batch and store the extra. Some recipes, like soups and braises, are barely more work at full size, and the leftovers freeze well. If you go that way, cool the extra portions quickly and freeze them in the sizes you will reheat. But if the recipe is a cake or a fiddly bake, scaling down to 2 is the better call.
